chunks: Ghiyāth ibn Ibrāhīm narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام, who said:
ʿAlī عليه السلام said: “Testimony upon testimony is not valid in a hadd, nor is kafālah valid in a hadd.”

key_terms.حَدٍّ: a prescribed legal punishment under Islamic law
key_terms.شَهَادَةٌ: legal testimony given by a witness
key_terms.عَلَى: upon; indicating one testimony being based on another
key_terms.كَفَالَةٌ: sponsorship or suretyship in a legal matter
key_terms.لَا تَجُوزُ: is not valid or permissible in legal effect

ai.seo_question: Are testimony upon testimony and kafalah valid in cases involving hudud in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning cases of prescribed punishments (hudud). It establishes that indirect testimony and kafalah are not accepted in hadd cases, indicating the strict evidentiary standards required in such judicial matters.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3356 - Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) from his father Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as):

Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) said: "Testimony upon testimony is not valid in cases involving prescribed punishments (hudud), nor is sponsorship (kafalah) valid in cases involving prescribed punishments."
